rationale: A is a greedy algorithm with a special-case tweak: prefer a 4-group over a 5-group when counts[4] < counts[2]. It is well commented, but its correctness rests on a hand-derived heuristic that is hard to verify and could break for basket shapes the tests do not cover. Reusing the name total for a local variable inside the function total is also a minor smell. B runs a memoized search over sorted count tuples. It considers every group size and states its one simplifying assumption (take from the tallest stacks) in a clear docstring, so it is clearly correct by construction and still efficient thanks to lru_cache. B is more robust and easier to trust, so it has the better code quality.
